query: For a selected high-entropy alloy whose superconducting behavior remains uncharacterized, what governs whether and how superconductivity emerges in the low-temperature test regime, and why? Propose one testable mechanistic hypothesis, a controlled comparison with the starting state, the observations expected relative to that baseline, the limits over which the hypothesis should hold, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Increasing the configurational entropy via targeted compositional alloying in a high-entropy alloy will promote superconductivity at low temperatures by inducing local lattice distortions that enhance electron–phonon coupling.
generation.material_initial_state: A high-entropy alloy in a single-phase, disordered solid-solution state with a moderate baseline configurational entropy and no or weak superconductivity at low temperatures.
generation.intervention: Engineer the alloy by adding one or more carefully selected elements to raise the configurational entropy (ΔSmix) without destabilizing the single-phase structure.
generation.conditions: Measurements performed in a low-temperature regime (typically below ~10 K) under controlled ambient pressures where the alloy remains structurally homogeneous.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced local lattice distortions and potential fluctuations arising from increased atomic-scale compositional disorder.
generation.mechanism: Elevating ΔSmix stabilizes a disordered lattice configuration that alters the phonon spectrum and local electron scattering. These changes can enhance electron–phonon interactions, leading to stronger pairing interactions and a measurable superconducting transition at low temperatures.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the baseline alloy with lower ΔSmix, the modified alloy should exhibit an increased superconducting transition temperature (Tc) and improved superconducting properties (for example, higher critical current densities) as a result of the enhanced electron–phonon coupling.
generation.baseline: A high-entropy alloy with less compositional diversity (and thus lower ΔSmix) that shows negligible or weak superconductivity in the low-temperature regime.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis is expected to hold when the increase in configurational entropy does not lead to phase separation or adverse electronic effects. Extremely high disorder, leading to loss of a coherent lattice or excessive carrier localization, could counteract the beneficial effects on electron–phonon coupling.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of Tc enhancement and the sensitivity of superconductivity to precise ΔSmix values are not well quantified. There is also uncertainty regarding the competing effects of potential carrier concentration imbalances that may arise from extensive alloying.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two sets of high-entropy alloy samples: one with relatively low ΔSmix (baseline composition) and one with increased ΔSmix achieved by adding additional, isostructural alloying elements. Process both sets under identical heat-treatment and synthesis conditions to ensure comparable microstructures. Cool samples to the low-temperature test regime and perform electrical resistance and magnetic susceptibility measurements.
measurements: Superconducting transition temperature (Tc) via resistance drop and diamagnetic onset
Critical current density (Jc) from magnetization measurements
Structural characterization (XRD/TEM) to verify single-phase nature and lattice distortions
Spectroscopic measurements that may indicate changes in electron–phonon coupling
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the high-entropy alloy with increased ΔSmix does not exhibit a higher Tc or improved superconducting properties relative to the baseline, or if the increase in ΔSmix results in phase separation or deleterious localization of charge carriers, then the hypothesis that engineered configurational entropy enhances superconductivity is falsified.

This characteristic can be explained by either the carrier concentration or the high-entropy effect. Even though the content of Ce4+ in the case of sample C is similar to that of the other samples, its slope of resistivity in the normal state region indicates that it has the lowest carrier concentration (Figure 5). The carrier concentration may have been reduced by the reduced carrier transfer from the RO layer to the BiS2 layer. A low carrier concentration can lower the transition temperature. The other possibility is that a high ΔSmix value can reduce Tc and decrease γs; also, a substantial-high-entropy effect can reduce superconducting anisotropy by inducing different local structures near the RO layer. The value of the upper critical field (Hc2) for sample C is the only one less than the Pauli limit (Hp), which is one of the deciding criteria for conventional or unconventional superconductors. REBa2Cu3O7-δ (RE123, RE: rare earth) is one of the high-temperature superconductors with a transition temperature (Tc) exceeding 90 K. Because of its high-Tc and large critical current density (Jc) under magnetic fields, RE123 superconductors have been expected to play a key role in superconductivity application. To accelerate application researches on RE123-based devices, further improvements of Jc characteristics have been desired. In this study, we investigated the effects of high-entropy alloying at the RE site on the superconducting properties, through the measurements of local (intra-grain) Jc (Jclocal) by a remanent magnetization method. We found that Jclocal shows a trend to be improved when four or five RE elements are mixed at the RE site, which results in high configurational entropy of mixing (ΔSmix). All samples exhibited an order of few MA cm−2 which is a criterion for practical application and the highest Jclocal resulted in a value of around 7.0 MA cm−2 at T = 2.0 K. Here, we reported the improvement of Jclocal in REBa2Cu3O7-d by the increase in ΔSmix at the RE site. Polycrystalline RE123 samples with different ΔSmix were synthesized by solid-state reaction. Through characterization of structural (lattice constants and OP), compositional and superconducting properties (Tc and shielding fraction), seven samples labelled RE-1–RE-7 were chosen, and remanent magnetization measurements were performed on those samples. At higher temperatures (T = 20.0 K), clear difference in Jclocal was not observed. At lower temperatures (T = 2.0 and 4.2 K), higher Jclocal was observed for RE-4 and RE-5 with a higher ΔSmix as compared with that for RE-1, RE-2, and RE-3 with zero or low entropy of mixing at the RE site. Although the results of the current work showed the merit of high-entropy alloying at lower temperatures only, there should be optimal conditions on constituent RE element, mixing ratio and ΔSmix, which will achieve higher Jclocal at higher temperatures as well. If the trial was achieved, the HEA concept can be applied to all RE123 practical materials to additionally improve their critical current properties.

chosen.approach: Engineer configurational entropy via compositional alloying modifications
